main_text.p: qua neminem morbu comitialem esse pas-surum ostendit Galenus, commentario in Aphorismum uicesimum octauum, Sectionis sextæ, Hippocratis: quæ uel intensa est, uel remissa: unde nonnulli celerius, & leuiori ex causa cum epilepsia conflictantur: alij uero tardius, & difficilius: quemadmodū arthriticis accidit, quorum articuli naturaliter sunt magis, aut minus debiles. Propterea epilepticorum cerebrum partim ex aëre frigido & humido, partim ex alimentis, & præsertim uaporosis, atq; etiam ex uino meraciori, aut uberius epoto materia sensim cogit ac generat, quâ sibi infensam persentiens sese comprimit, ut eam excludat. Atq; hoc pacto singuli epilepsiæ paroxysmi excitari solent. Animalis enim facultas, ut à sese obstruentis materiæ noxam repellat, cum humore, aut uapore terro colluctatur: unde spasmo quatiuntur epileptici. Quapropter ipsi nec audiunt, nec uident, neq; ullo modo sentiunt, neq; memorantur, neque quicquam imaginantur: nec deniq; intelligunt, caligate anima: propterea quòd animalis spiritus in cerebri finibus à crassa materia & uiscida obstruente, quæ interdū pituitosa est, interdum melancholica, prohibe-

page.notes: Handwritten marginal annotation in the right margin, in ink, not printed: not transcribed. A printed underline runs under "Animalis" in the text, which is noted here only. The word "quâ" carries a mark over the a, transcribed as printed. The last line ends with the hyphenated fragment "prohibe-", which continues on the next page. The text is in a mix of long-s forms, transcribed as plain s.
